## BUILDER CONTEXT
# Builder Profile — Sam

## Role
Solo founder and full-stack engineer. Building across multiple projects simultaneously.
Primary consumer of all generated specs — implementation guides must be self-contained.

## Active Projects (2026)
- **sam-plugin** — personal OpenClaw plugin (this project); wires agent to Sam's live systems
- **spec-doc** — this tool (Flask :3101 + Angular :4201); documentation-first dev methodology
- **humanize-me** — live Flask + Next.js AI humanizer; production at humaniz.me
- **Bubls** — Ionic + Capacitor mobile app (event discovery, Zürich); Angular + Flask
- **Trendfy** — wardrobai/trendfy.me; AI fashion photoshoot; kill date passed, status TBD
- **OpenClaw** — local AI agent gateway; runs claude-cli provider, Telegram-connected

## Stack Preferences
- **Backend**: Python / Flask (thin, ~150 lines, Blueprints, openapi.yaml-first)
- **Frontend (web)**: Angular (standalone components, signals) or Next.js 15 + shadcn/ui
- **Frontend (mobile)**: Ionic + Capacitor (iOS 16+, Angular)
- **AI**: Claude CLI (dev) → Anthropic SDK (prod); chain adapter pattern
- **Deploy**: Docker Compose → Coolify; single gunicorn + nginx pattern
- **Agent platform**: OpenClaw (local gateway, claude-cli provider, Telegram channel)

## Engineering Preferences
- Brain dump → AI structures it → ship. Minimal viable shape, not maximum abstraction
- Small focused modules with clear boundaries — no god classes, no god files
- Adapter pattern for all external services (AI, DB, storage)
- In-process state (module-level dict + threading.Lock) is fine for single-consumer async
- No speculative abstractions — build for the one concrete case that exists now
- Files under 200 lines; named exports; one component per file
- Build order: frontend with mock data first → Flask built to match the UI's API contract

## Known Constraints
- Solo developer — no handoff; guides must be runnable by one person end-to-end
- No Redis, no Postgres (unless Supabase via Flask), no external queue
- Claude CLI subprocess timeout: 3600s; Anthropic SDK: no practical ceiling
- OpenClaw workspace plugin system: skills first (SKILL.md files), graduate to full plugin when needed
- Telegram is the primary mobile interface — responses must stay under 4096 chars


## ARCHITECTURE PRINCIPLES (non-negotiable — follow these patterns)
# Engineering Principles — Sam's Projects

Non-negotiable across all projects. When a brain dump contradicts a principle, the analysis step must flag it.

## P1 — Adapter Boundary
All external service calls (AI, DB, storage, HTTP) go through a single adapter module.
No feature code imports a provider directly. The adapter is the only file that knows which provider is active.
- spec-doc: `modules/chain/adapter.py`
- OpenClaw plugins: wrap external calls in a dedicated skill or tool wrapper

## P2 — Thin HTTP Layer
Route handlers contain no business logic. Handlers: validate input → call service → return response.
- Flask: `routes.py` handles HTTP only; `service.py` holds pure Python logic
- OpenClaw: skill files describe tool invocations; no inline logic

## P3 — Async 202 + Polling for Long Operations
Any operation > 30s returns 202 immediately with a job identifier.
A background thread does the work. A status endpoint lets the client poll until `done: true`.
No HTTP connection held open. No Redis — in-process state keyed by job/project id.

## P4 — No Speculative Abstractions
Build for the one concrete case that exists now. No generic runners for one consumer.
No base classes for one subclass. No registries for one item.
Three similar lines of code is better than a premature abstraction.

## P5 — OpenAPI-First (spec-doc)
`openapi.yaml` is the contract. DTOs are generated from it. Never hand-edit generated files.
Routes implement the contract — not the other way around.

## P6 — OpenClaw Plugin Principles
- Skills first: start with `SKILL.md` files (no build step, iterate fast)
- Graduate to `openclaw.plugin.json` package only when skills hit real limits
- References are the single source of truth — no rules duplicated inline in agents/skills
- Agents are declarative descriptions, not imperative code
- Context files (`MEMORY.md`, `USER.md`, `TOOLS.md`) are loaded every session — keep them current
- Boot hooks fire on session start — keep them cheap (no blocking I/O)
- Channel-aware: skills must adjust output format per channel (Telegram ≠ web UI)

## P7 — File Size & Structure
- Files under 200 lines (hard target, not a guideline)
- Named exports only (no default exports in Angular/TS)
- One component per file
- Build verification required before each commit (Angular: `ng build --configuration production`)

## Code Rules
- No direct push to master — always PRs; PRs target master; live is deploy branch
- Daemon threads only (`daemon=True`) — never block server shutdown
- Empty context strings handled gracefully — callers never crash on missing context
- `read_context()` returns `""` for missing files; `PromptBuilder.section()` skips empty content


## CONTEXT FROM EPIC (generated in prior step)
# 🎯 Epic: Thin API Phase 3

## Business Value

Spec-doc's frontend currently embeds AI instruction strings directly in `ai.service.ts`, meaning every prompt tweak requires a full Angular rebuild and deploy. Nine distinct user actions (brainstorm, expand, compress, clarify, simplify, tldr, bullets, rewrite, styleAs) all funnel through a single `/api/ai/text/rewrite` endpoint with the actual instructions concatenated client-side. This couples prompt engineering to frontend release cycles and leaks AI behavior knowledge into a layer that should know nothing about it.

Phase 3 flips the contract: action-named flat endpoints (`/api/brainstorm`, `/api/expand`, …) where the frontend sends `{ text }` and receives `{ text, latencyMs }`. SKILL.md files become the single source of truth for prompts. The Angular client is generated from `openapi.yaml` via `ng-openapi-gen`, eliminating ~400 LOC of hand-written HTTP code and ~423 LOC of Python prompt strings.

The payoff is iteration velocity: tuning a prompt becomes a SKILL.md edit on the backend — no frontend deploy, no TypeScript change, no rebuild. Adding a new text action becomes a three-step pattern (openapi.yaml entry + SKILL.md + 10-line Flask route). For a solo founder shipping spec-doc as a documentation-first tool, this is the difference between "AI behavior is a deploy" and "AI behavior is a file edit."

## Scope

### What This Epic Covers

- **Flat action-named API surface** — 8 routes under `/api/text/<action>` (brainstorm, expand, compress, clarify, simplify, tldr, bullets, rewrite) replacing the single overloaded `/api/ai/text/rewrite` endpoint
- **SKILL.md authorship** — create missing SKILL.md files for expand, compress, clarify, simplify, tldr, bullets; verify existing brainstorm and rewrite skills handle their inputs
- **OpenAPI-first contract** — `openapi.yaml` defines all 8 routes; `style` enum lives in the schema; `ng-openapi-gen` produces the Angular client
- **Generated Angular client** — `ai.service.ts` rewritten as a thin wrapper over the generated client; zero hardcoded instruction strings
- **Brainstorm-followup consolidation** — `app.component.ts` stops assembling prompt strings; `/api/text/brainstorm` accepts optional `{ question, context }` and the SKILL.md branches on presence
- **Backend cleanup** — delete `text_prompts.py` (423 LOC), the `/api/ai/text/rewrite` and `/api/ai/text/generate` routes, and all associated tests once cutover is verified

### What This Epic Does NOT Cover

- ❌ **Bootstrap-project and generate-epic-guide migration** — async multi-step chains; deferred to Phase 4 (resolves the braindump contradiction)
- ❌ **`task_gen.py` deletion** — still used by active routes; audit separately
- ❌ **`quality/` module refactor** — still in use; audit separately
- ❌ **Removing unused routes (`iterate`, `lint-braindump`, `review`)** — unrelated cleanup; ship as a separate PR
- ❌ **New text actions beyond the 8 listed** — no speculative endpoints
- ❌ **Auth, billing, project CRUD changes** — untouched
- ❌ **URL-prefix re-litigation** — settled at `/api/text/<action>` (matches the Angular sample and followup section)

## Tasks

| # | Task | Dependencies | Parallel | Effort | Priority |
|---|------|--------------|----------|--------|----------|
| 1 | **Define OpenAPI contract for 8 text actions** | None | — | 0.5 day | High |
| 2 | **Author missing SKILL.md files** (expand, compress, clarify, simplify, tldr, bullets) | None | Yes (with #1) | 1 day | High |
| 3 | **Implement 8 thin Flask routes under `/api/text`** | 1, 2 | — | 1 day | High |
| 4 | **Generate Angular client and rewrite `ai.service.ts`** | 1, 3 | — | 1 day | High |
| 5 | **Cut over frontend, verify end-to-end, delete dead Python and TypeScript** | 4 | — | 0.5 day | High |

## Success Criteria

- ✅ Frontend ships zero instruction strings, zero system prompts, zero `style`-to-prompt mapping logic
- ✅ All 8 text actions reachable at `POST /api/text/<action>` and returning `{ text, latencyMs }`
- ✅ `ai.service.ts` is under 50 LOC and delegates to the `ng-openapi-gen` generated client
- ✅ Each Flask route handler is under 15 LOC (validate → call skill → return)
- ✅ `openapi.yaml` is the contract — `style` enum defined there, DTOs generated from it
- ✅ `text_prompts.py`, `/api/ai/text/rewrite`, `/api/ai/text/generate`, and their tests removed from the repo
- ✅ `app.component.ts` no longer assembles brainstorm-followup instruction strings
- ✅ Adding a hypothetical 9th action requires only: openapi.yaml entry + SKILL.md + Flask route (no frontend prompt code)
- ✅ Production Angular build passes (`ng build --configuration production`)

## Related Documents

- [Analysis](./analysis.md) – Problems driving this epic
- [Solution Architecture](./architecture.md) – System design
- [Timeline](./timeline.md) – Status tracking

Design the solution architecture to fulfill the tasks and scope defined above.

## Chain Adapter

## REFERENCE CODE (port from, not code in the target repo)
# Reference Code — Patterns to Port

These are real working patterns from sibling projects. When architecture says "port from references.md",
describe the shape to port — not the implementation detail.

## financing-plugin — Claude Code Plugin Structure

The gold standard for a well-structured Claude Code plugin.
Location: `~/Projects/financing-plugin-extracted/`

### Plugin Layout Pattern
```
plugin-name/
├── .claude-plugin/plugin.json   # Plugin metadata + version
├── agents/                      # Specialised agents as flat .md files
├── hooks/                       # SessionStart hook (context injection)
├── references/                  # Convention references (single source of truth)
├── skills/                      # Skills — each a SKILL.md
│   ├── SKILL_MAP.md             # Master index of all skills
│   ├── feature-pipeline/SKILL.md   # Orchestrator skill
│   ├── feature-requirement/SKILL.md
│   └── dev-build/SKILL.md       # Dev tools
└── docs/                        # Spec-doc specs (Epic, Architecture)
```

Key rule: **references are the source of truth** — no rules duplicated inline in agents/skills.
Skills read from `references/*.md`, never inline the same constraint twice.

### SessionStart Hook Pattern
The hook fires on every session start and injects live context into the agent.
No heavy I/O — just read files and compute a snapshot. Fast and deterministic.

### Skill File Pattern (SKILL.md)
```markdown
# Skill Name

## When to use
[Trigger conditions]

## What I do
[Steps the agent takes]

## Tools available
[Bash, Read, Write, etc.]

## Examples
[Sample invocations]
```

## OpenClaw Workspace Files — Context Injection Pattern

The workspace files already loaded by OpenClaw every session:
- `AGENTS.md` — session instructions (auto-loaded)
- `USER.md` — who Sam is (auto-loaded)
- `MEMORY.md` — curated long-term memory (auto-loaded in main session)
- `TOOLS.md` — stack + environment (auto-loaded)

Port pattern: new skills should reference these files rather than duplicating their content.
`SOUL.md` defines agent identity — skills can refer to it for tone/style.

## spec-doc Bootstrap Adapter — Async 202 + Polling Pattern

Already shipping in spec-doc. Port this pattern for any long-running skill:
1. POST trigger → return 202 + job_id immediately
2. Background thread runs the work
3. GET /status/{job_id} polls until `done: true`
4. In-process dict keyed by project/job id — no Redis needed

Location: `~/Projects/2026/spec-doc/api/modules/ai/routes/text.py` (bootstrap)
and `~/Projects/2026/spec-doc/api/modules/ai/routes/task_gen.py` (generate-task)

## Trendfy — Docker + Deploy Pattern

gunicorn config for Flask with background threads:
```
gunicorn --bind 0.0.0.0:3101 --workers 1 --threads 4 --timeout 900 --worker-class gthread
```
`--workers 1` required when using in-process state dicts (no cross-worker sharing).
`gthread` allows daemon threads to coexist with gunicorn.

## humanize-me — Flask Thin Layer Pattern

Flask as a ~150 line AI service boundary:
- All routes: validate → call AI adapter → return streaming or JSON
- No business logic in routes
- Supabase accessed only through Flask, never from frontend directly


## CONTENT ROUTING RULES (violations are failures)
- Status words (Done, In Progress, Completed) → ONLY in timeline.md
- Code blocks with implementation → ONLY in implementation guides
- Business value and market analysis → ONLY in epic.md
- Design decisions and tech stack → ONLY in architecture.md
- Step-by-step instructions → ONLY in implementation guides
- Problem identification → ONLY in analysis.md
- Cross-references MUST be bidirectional (if A→B then B→A)
- Always use "Solution Architecture" (not just "Architecture") in cross-references
## Your ONE Job
System design, decisions, trade-offs. NO code blocks. NO status.

## Output Format
OUTPUT ONLY markdown. Start with #. No preamble.

# Thin API Phase 3 — Braindump

## What this is

Phase 3 of the thin API migration. Phase 2 added the generic skill infrastructure (SKILL.md files, generic skill route). Phase 3 is about:

1. Clean, flat, action-named API contract — routes are `/api/brainstorm`, `/api/expand`, etc. No `/text/` or `/ai/` prefix.
2. Frontend becomes dumb — sends data, gets result, knows nothing about prompts or skills
3. All instruction complexity moves to the backend (Python route → skill → SKILL.md → Claude)
4. Angular API client generated from OpenAPI spec — no hand-written HTTP code in the frontend
5. Delete as much Python as possible — migrate all AI routes to skills, including `bootstrap-project` and `generate-epic-guide`

## The problem with the current frontend

`ai.service.ts` today has the brainstorm prompt instructions hardcoded in TypeScript:

```ts
brainstorm(text: string): Promise<TextOperationResponse> {
  return this.rewrite(text, [
    'You are a product thinking partner. Given this raw brain dump, generate a structured brainstorm response...',
    '1. **Key Themes** — ...',
    ...
  ].join('
'));
}
```

This is wrong. Prompt engineering in TypeScript means:
- Prompts can't be improved without a frontend deploy
- The frontend is aware of AI instructions — it shouldn't be
- All the expand/compress/clarify/simplify/tldr/bullets variants are just `rewrite()` with different instruction strings baked in TypeScript

The fix: each action gets a named flat endpoint. The backend owns the instructions. Frontend sends `{ text }` and gets `{ text, latencyMs }`.

## Current API surface (frontend perspective)

### What the frontend actually calls today

**ai.service.ts:**
- `POST /api/ai/text/rewrite` — used for rewrite, expand, compress, clarify, simplify, tldr, bullets, brainstorm, styleAs (all same endpoint, different instruction strings)
- `POST /api/ai/text/generate` — generic text generation with `{ prompt, tone }`

**projects.service.ts:**
- `POST /api/ai/text/bootstrap-project` — async spec generation (multi-step AI chain)
- `GET /api/ai/text/bootstrap-project/status/<job_id>` — poll bootstrap
- `POST /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide` — async epic guide generation
- `GET /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide/status` — poll epic guide
- `GET /api/projects` — list projects
- `GET /api/projects/<id>` — get project
- `POST /api/projects` — create project
- `PUT /api/projects/<id>/files/<filename>` — save file

## Target API contract — flat, action-named routes

### Text operations (new — replaces the single /rewrite endpoint)

Each action is its own route. No `/text/` or `/ai/` prefix — just the verb. Backend owns all prompt logic.

```
POST /api/brainstorm   { text, question?, context? }  → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/expand       { text }                        → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/compress     { text }                        → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/clarify      { text }                        → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/simplify     { text }                        → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/tldr         { text }                        → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/bullets      { text }                        → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/rewrite      { text, style }                 → { text, latencyMs }
```

`style` values for `/rewrite`: Concise | Technical | Executive | Narrative | Punchy. Backend maps these to Claude instructions. Frontend doesn't know what those instructions say.

No `/generate` endpoint — it's not used for a clear business action. Remove.

### Angular API client

Generated from `openapi.yaml` using `ng-openapi-gen`. No hand-written HTTP code. `ai.service.ts` is replaced by the generated client. Adding a new action = update openapi.yaml + add SKILL.md + add Flask route. Frontend regenerates automatically.

### Project management (unchanged)

```
GET    /api/projects
POST   /api/projects
GET    /api/projects/<id>
PUT    /api/projects/<id>/files/<filename>
```

### Spec generation (migrate to skills in Phase 3)

`bootstrap-project` and `generate-epic-guide` are multi-step async chains currently implemented in Python. Phase 3 migrates these to skill pipelines — the full chain (analysis → epic → architecture → timeline) runs via SKILL.md + agent, not Python service code. The endpoints stay but the Python behind them becomes a thin job dispatcher.

```
POST   /api/bootstrap          { project_name, braindump }  → { job_id }
GET    /api/bootstrap/<job_id>                               → { done, files, current_step }
POST   /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide               → { job_id }
GET    /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide/status        → { done, filename }
```

## Backend implementation

Each new `/api/text/<action>` route is a thin Python handler:
- Auth check
- Extract `text` from body (+ `style` for rewrite)
- Call the corresponding skill (which calls SKILL.md → Claude)
- Return `{ text, latencyMs }`

The skills already exist or need creating:
- `brainstorm` skill — exists in plugin/skills/
- `rewrite` skill — exists in plugin/skills/
- `expand`, `compress`, `clarify`, `simplify`, `tldr`, `bullets` — may need SKILL.md files created

The Python routes are ~10 lines each. The intelligence lives in SKILL.md.

## What gets deleted

Once the new `/api/<action>` routes are live and the frontend is updated:

### Dead Python routes in text.py
- `POST /api/ai/text/rewrite` — replaced by individual action routes
- `POST /api/ai/text/generate` — removed, no equivalent needed
- `POST /api/ai/text/iterate` — was never called from frontend
- `POST /api/ai/text/lint-braindump` — was never called from frontend
- `POST /api/ai/text/review` — was never called from frontend

### Dead Python files (once routes and bootstrap are migrated)
- `api/modules/ai/services/text_prompts.py` (423 LOC) — all prompt strings
- `api/modules/ai/services/task_gen.py` (537 LOC) — most of it, once bootstrap is a skill pipeline
- `api/modules/ai/workflows/spec_gen/` — Python AI workflow chains replaced by skills
- Their test files

### Dead TypeScript
- `ai.service.ts` — replaced entirely by generated OpenAPI client
- All instruction strings, the `generate()` method, the base URL constants

## What stays

- `bootstrap-project` and `generate-epic-guide` routes (async, complex — Phase 4)
- `quality/` module (still in use by active routes — audit separately)
- `task_gen.py` service (still in use by active routes — audit separately)
- All auth, billing, project CRUD

## What the Angular service looks like after

```typescript
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class AiService {
  private readonly base = '/api/text';
  constructor(private http: HttpClient) {}

  brainstorm(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('brainstorm', { text });
  }
  expand(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('expand', { text });
  }
  compress(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('compress', { text });
  }
  clarify(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('clarify', { text });
  }
  simplify(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('simplify', { text });
  }
  tldr(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('tldr', { text });
  }
  bullets(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('bullets', { text });
  }
  rewrite(text: string, style: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('rewrite', { text, style });
  }

  private post(action: string, body: object): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return firstValueFrom(
      this.http.post<TextResponse>(`${this.base}/${action}`, body)
        .pipe(timeout(AI_TIMEOUT_MS))
    );
  }
}
```

No instruction strings. No prompt logic. Each method is ~3 lines.

The `followupBrainstorm()` method in `app.component.ts` currently assembles context and sends a custom rewrite instruction. After Phase 3, this becomes a call to a dedicated `POST /api/text/brainstorm-followup` route, or the brainstorm skill handles the follow-up via the same `/api/text/brainstorm` endpoint with additional context in the body.

## Architectural principle — facade

The API is a facade. The frontend:
- Has zero instruction strings
- Has zero system prompts
- Has zero AI behavior knowledge
- Sends data, receives results

Every AI decision — what the prompt says, how Claude should respond, what context to include — lives in the backend. SKILL.md is the source of truth. Python routes are the facade surface.

This also resolves the followup brainstorm pattern. Currently `app.component.ts` assembles:
```ts
`You are a brainstorming partner. The user wants to explore: "${question}"
...`
```
That instruction string is eliminated. The endpoint becomes:
```
POST /api/text/brainstorm  { text, question?, context? }  → { text, latencyMs }
```
The SKILL.md decides what to do when `question` is present vs. absent. Frontend sends the data structure, knows nothing about what happens next.

Same principle for style/rewrite: frontend sends `{ text, style: "Concise" }`. Backend maps "Concise" to Claude instructions. Frontend doesn't know what "Concise" means to Claude.

## Sequence

1. Create SKILL.md files for expand, compress, clarify, simplify, tldr, bullets (if they don't exist)
2. Add Python blueprint `/api/text` with 8 route handlers (thin, call skills)
3. Update `ai.service.ts` — new base URL, clean methods, no instruction strings
4. Test end-to-end
5. Delete old `/api/ai/text/rewrite`, `/api/ai/text/generate` routes
6. Delete `text_prompts.py` and its tests
7. Delete dead TypeScript

Focus on WHY. Explain trade-offs. No code blocks.

# Engineering Principles — Sam's Projects

Non-negotiable across all projects. When a brain dump contradicts a principle, the analysis step must flag it.

## P1 — Adapter Boundary
All external service calls (AI, DB, storage, HTTP) go through a single adapter module.
No feature code imports a provider directly. The adapter is the only file that knows which provider is active.
- spec-doc: `modules/chain/adapter.py`
- OpenClaw plugins: wrap external calls in a dedicated skill or tool wrapper

## P2 — Thin HTTP Layer
Route handlers contain no business logic. Handlers: validate input → call service → return response.
- Flask: `routes.py` handles HTTP only; `service.py` holds pure Python logic
- OpenClaw: skill files describe tool invocations; no inline logic

## P3 — Async 202 + Polling for Long Operations
Any operation > 30s returns 202 immediately with a job identifier.
A background thread does the work. A status endpoint lets the client poll until `done: true`.
No HTTP connection held open. No Redis — in-process state keyed by job/project id.

## P4 — No Speculative Abstractions
Build for the one concrete case that exists now. No generic runners for one consumer.
No base classes for one subclass. No registries for one item.
Three similar lines of code is better than a premature abstraction.

## P5 — OpenAPI-First (spec-doc)
`openapi.yaml` is the contract. DTOs are generated from it. Never hand-edit generated files.
Routes implement the contract — not the other way around.

- References are the single source of truth — no rules duplicated inline in agents/skills

- Context files (`MEMORY.md`, `USER.md`, `TOOLS.md`) are loaded every session — keep them current
- Boot hooks fire on session start — keep them cheap (no blocking I/O)

- Named exports only (no default exports in Angular/TS)
- One component per file
- Build verification required before each commit (Angular: `ng build --configuration production`)

- Daemon threads only (`daemon=True`) — never block server shutdown
- Empty context strings handled gracefully — callers never crash on missing context

# 🎯 Epic: Thin API Phase 3

## Business Value

Spec-doc's frontend currently embeds AI instruction strings directly in `ai.service.ts`, meaning every prompt tweak requires a full Angular rebuild and deploy. Nine distinct user actions (brainstorm, expand, compress, clarify, simplify, tldr, bullets, rewrite, styleAs) all funnel through a single `/api/ai/text/rewrite` endpoint with the actual instructions concatenated client-side. This couples prompt engineering to frontend release cycles and leaks AI behavior knowledge into a layer that should know nothing about it.

Phase 3 flips the contract: action-named flat endpoints (`/api/brainstorm`, `/api/expand`, …) where the frontend sends `{ text }` and receives `{ text, latencyMs }`. SKILL.md files become the single source of truth for prompts. The Angular client is generated from `openapi.yaml` via `ng-openapi-gen`, eliminating ~400 LOC of hand-written HTTP code and ~423 LOC of Python prompt strings.

The payoff is iteration velocity: tuning a prompt becomes a SKILL.md edit on the backend — no frontend deploy, no TypeScript change, no rebuild. Adding a new text action becomes a three-step pattern (openapi.yaml entry + SKILL.md + 10-line Flask route). For a solo founder shipping spec-doc as a documentation-first tool, this is the difference between "AI behavior is a deploy" and "AI behavior is a file edit."

## Scope

### What This Epic Covers

- **Flat action-named API surface** — 8 routes under `/api/text/<action>` (brainstorm, expand, compress, clarify, simplify, tldr, bullets, rewrite) replacing the single overloaded `/api/ai/text/rewrite` endpoint
- **SKILL.md authorship** — create missing SKILL.md files for expand, compress, clarify, simplify, tldr, bullets; verify existing brainstorm and rewrite skills handle their inputs
- **OpenAPI-first contract** — `openapi.yaml` defines all 8 routes; `style` enum lives in the schema; `ng-openapi-gen` produces the Angular client
- **Generated Angular client** — `ai.service.ts` rewritten as a thin wrapper over the generated client; zero hardcoded instruction strings
- **Brainstorm-followup consolidation** — `app.component.ts` stops assembling prompt strings; `/api/text/brainstorm` accepts optional `{ question, context }` and the SKILL.md branches on presence
- **Backend cleanup** — delete `text_prompts.py` (423 LOC), the `/api/ai/text/rewrite` and `/api/ai/text/generate` routes, and all associated tests once cutover is verified

### What This Epic Does NOT Cover

- ❌ **Bootstrap-project and generate-epic-guide migration** — async multi-step chains; deferred to Phase 4 (resolves the braindump contradiction)
- ❌ **`task_gen.py` deletion** — still used by active routes; audit separately
- ❌ **`quality/` module refactor** — still in use; audit separately
- ❌ **Removing unused routes (`iterate`, `lint-braindump`, `review`)** — unrelated cleanup; ship as a separate PR
- ❌ **New text actions beyond the 8 listed** — no speculative endpoints
- ❌ **Auth, billing, project CRUD changes** — untouched
- ❌ **URL-prefix re-litigation** — settled at `/api/text/<action>` (matches the Angular sample and followup section)

## Success Criteria

# Thin API Phase 3 — Braindump

## What this is

Phase 3 of the thin API migration. Phase 2 added the generic skill infrastructure (SKILL.md files, generic skill route). Phase 3 is about:

1. Clean, flat, action-named API contract — routes are `/api/brainstorm`, `/api/expand`, etc. No `/text/` or `/ai/` prefix.
2. Frontend becomes dumb — sends data, gets result, knows nothing about prompts or skills
3. All instruction complexity moves to the backend (Python route → skill → SKILL.md → Claude)
4. Angular API client generated from OpenAPI spec — no hand-written HTTP code in the frontend
5. Delete as much Python as possible — migrate all AI routes to skills, including `bootstrap-project` and `generate-epic-guide`

## The problem with the current frontend

`ai.service.ts` today has the brainstorm prompt instructions hardcoded in TypeScript:

```ts
brainstorm(text: string): Promise<TextOperationResponse> {
  return this.rewrite(text, [
    'You are a product thinking partner. Given this raw brain dump, generate a structured brainstorm response...',
    '1. **Key Themes** — ...',
    ...
  ].join('
'));
}
```

This is wrong. Prompt engineering in TypeScript means:
- Prompts can't be improved without a frontend deploy
- The frontend is aware of AI instructions — it shouldn't be
- All the expand/compress/clarify/simplify/tldr/bullets variants are just `rewrite()` with different instruction strings baked in TypeScript

The fix: each action gets a named flat endpoint. The backend owns the instructions. Frontend sends `{ text }` and gets `{ text, latencyMs }`.

## Current API surface (frontend perspective)

### What the frontend actually calls today

**ai.service.ts:**
- `POST /api/ai/text/rewrite` — used for rewrite, expand, compress, clarify, simplify, tldr, bullets, brainstorm, styleAs (all same endpoint, different instruction strings)
- `POST /api/ai/text/generate` — generic text generation with `{ prompt, tone }`

**projects.service.ts:**
- `POST /api/ai/text/bootstrap-project` — async spec generation (multi-step AI chain)
- `GET /api/ai/text/bootstrap-project/status/<job_id>` — poll bootstrap
- `POST /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide` — async epic guide generation
- `GET /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide/status` — poll epic guide
- `GET /api/projects` — list projects
- `GET /api/projects/<id>` — get project
- `POST /api/projects` — create project
- `PUT /api/projects/<id>/files/<filename>` — save file

## Target API contract — flat, action-named routes

### Text operations (new — replaces the single /rewrite endpoint)

Each action is its own route. No `/text/` or `/ai/` prefix — just the verb. Backend owns all prompt logic.

```
POST /api/brainstorm   { text, question?, context? }  → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/expand       { text }                        → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/compress     { text }                        → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/clarify      { text }                        → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/simplify     { text }                        → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/tldr         { text }                        → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/bullets      { text }                        → { text, latencyMs }
POST /api/rewrite      { text, style }                 → { text, latencyMs }
```

`style` values for `/rewrite`: Concise | Technical | Executive | Narrative | Punchy. Backend maps these to Claude instructions. Frontend doesn't know what those instructions say.

No `/generate` endpoint — it's not used for a clear business action. Remove.

### Angular API client

Generated from `openapi.yaml` using `ng-openapi-gen`. No hand-written HTTP code. `ai.service.ts` is replaced by the generated client. Adding a new action = update openapi.yaml + add SKILL.md + add Flask route. Frontend regenerates automatically.

### Project management (unchanged)

```
GET    /api/projects
POST   /api/projects
GET    /api/projects/<id>
PUT    /api/projects/<id>/files/<filename>
```

### Spec generation (migrate to skills in Phase 3)

`bootstrap-project` and `generate-epic-guide` are multi-step async chains currently implemented in Python. Phase 3 migrates these to skill pipelines — the full chain (analysis → epic → architecture → timeline) runs via SKILL.md + agent, not Python service code. The endpoints stay but the Python behind them becomes a thin job dispatcher.

```
POST   /api/bootstrap          { project_name, braindump }  → { job_id }
GET    /api/bootstrap/<job_id>                               → { done, files, current_step }
POST   /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide               → { job_id }
GET    /api/projects/<id>/generate-epic-guide/status        → { done, filename }
```

## Backend implementation

Each new `/api/text/<action>` route is a thin Python handler:
- Auth check
- Extract `text` from body (+ `style` for rewrite)
- Call the corresponding skill (which calls SKILL.md → Claude)
- Return `{ text, latencyMs }`

The skills already exist or need creating:
- `brainstorm` skill — exists in plugin/skills/
- `rewrite` skill — exists in plugin/skills/
- `expand`, `compress`, `clarify`, `simplify`, `tldr`, `bullets` — may need SKILL.md files created

The Python routes are ~10 lines each. The intelligence lives in SKILL.md.

## What gets deleted

Once the new `/api/<action>` routes are live and the frontend is updated:

### Dead Python routes in text.py
- `POST /api/ai/text/rewrite` — replaced by individual action routes
- `POST /api/ai/text/generate` — removed, no equivalent needed
- `POST /api/ai/text/iterate` — was never called from frontend
- `POST /api/ai/text/lint-braindump` — was never called from frontend
- `POST /api/ai/text/review` — was never called from frontend

### Dead Python files (once routes and bootstrap are migrated)
- `api/modules/ai/services/text_prompts.py` (423 LOC) — all prompt strings
- `api/modules/ai/services/task_gen.py` (537 LOC) — most of it, once bootstrap is a skill pipeline
- `api/modules/ai/workflows/spec_gen/` — Python AI workflow chains replaced by skills
- Their test files

### Dead TypeScript
- `ai.service.ts` — replaced entirely by generated OpenAPI client
- All instruction strings, the `generate()` method, the base URL constants

## What stays

- `bootstrap-project` and `generate-epic-guide` routes (async, complex — Phase 4)
- `quality/` module (still in use by active routes — audit separately)
- `task_gen.py` service (still in use by active routes — audit separately)
- All auth, billing, project CRUD

## What the Angular service looks like after

```typescript
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class AiService {
  private readonly base = '/api/text';
  constructor(private http: HttpClient) {}

  brainstorm(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('brainstorm', { text });
  }
  expand(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('expand', { text });
  }
  compress(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('compress', { text });
  }
  clarify(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('clarify', { text });
  }
  simplify(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {

  }
  tldr(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {

  }
  bullets(text: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('bullets', { text });
  }
  rewrite(text: string, style: string): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return this.post('rewrite', { text, style });
  }

  private post(action: string, body: object): Promise<TextResponse> {
    return firstValueFrom(
      this.http.post<TextResponse>(`${this.base}/${action}`, body)

```

No instruction strings. No prompt logic. Each method is ~3 lines.

The `followupBrainstorm()` method in `app.component.ts` currently assembles context and sends a custom rewrite instruction. After Phase 3, this becomes a call to a dedicated `POST /api/text/brainstorm-followup` route, or the brainstorm skill handles the follow-up via the same `/api/text/brainstorm` endpoint with additional context in the body.

## Architectural principle — facade

The API is a facade. The frontend:
- Has zero instruction strings
- Has zero system prompts
- Has zero AI behavior knowledge
- Sends data, receives results

Every AI decision — what the prompt says, how Claude should respond, what context to include — lives in the backend. SKILL.md is the source of truth. Python routes are the facade surface.

```ts

...`
```
That instruction string is eliminated. The endpoint becomes:
```
POST /api/text/brainstorm  { text, question?, context? }  → { text, latencyMs }
```
The SKILL.md decides what to do when `question` is present vs. absent. Frontend sends the data structure, knows nothing about what happens next.

Same principle for style/rewrite: frontend sends `{ text, style: "Concise" }`. Backend maps "Concise" to Claude instructions. Frontend doesn't know what "Concise" means to Claude.

## Sequence

1. Create SKILL.md files for expand, compress, clarify, simplify, tldr, bullets (if they don't exist)
2. Add Python blueprint `/api/text` with 8 route handlers (thin, call skills)
3. Update `ai.service.ts` — new base URL, clean methods, no instruction strings
4. Test end-to-end

content.text:
# 🏗️ Solution Architecture: Thin API Phase 3

## Architecture Overview

Phase 3 inverts the prompt ownership boundary. Today, the Angular frontend assembles instruction strings in TypeScript and posts them through a single overloaded `/api/ai/text/rewrite` endpoint — the backend is a passthrough, the frontend is the prompt engineer. The new model treats the API as a **facade**: action-named flat routes (`POST /api/text/<action>`) where the frontend sends structured data (`{ text }`, `{ text, style }`, `{ text, question?, context? }`) and receives `{ text, latencyMs }`. The backend owns every AI decision via SKILL.md files; the frontend owns presentation.

The mental model is a three-layer stack with one source of truth at each layer. `openapi.yaml` is the contract — it defines all 8 routes, the `style` enum, and the request/response DTOs. SKILL.md files are the prompt source — one per action, edited without redeploy. Flask routes are thin adapters — validate, call the skill via the chain adapter, return. The Angular client is generated from `openapi.yaml` via `ng-openapi-gen`, so adding an action becomes a mechanical three-step pattern with no hand-written HTTP code, no embedded instruction strings, and no `style`-to-prompt mapping in TypeScript.

The key insight is that **prompt engineering velocity is gated by the slowest deploy in the chain**. When prompts live in TypeScript, every tweak requires an Angular rebuild, a static asset push, and cache busting. When prompts live in SKILL.md, a tweak is a file edit on the backend — picked up by the next Claude CLI invocation. Phase 3 trades a small amount of route boilerplate (8 routes × ~10 LOC) for ~423 LOC of deletable Python (`text_prompts.py`), ~400 LOC of deletable hand-written HTTP code, and a permanent shift in iteration cost.

## Design Principles

| Principle | Application |
|-----------|-------------|
| **P1 — Adapter Boundary** | All AI calls flow through `modules/runtime/chain/adapter.py`. Each text route invokes the chain adapter with the SKILL.md path; no provider imports leak into route or service code. |
| **P2 — Thin HTTP Layer** | Every route handler under `/api/text/<action>` is auth-check → validate body → delegate to skill → return DTO. Target ≤15 LOC per handler, no branching on action type, no business logic. |
| **P4 — No Speculative Abstractions** | Eight concrete routes, eight concrete SKILL.md files. No `ActionRegistry`, no `BaseTextRoute`, no dispatcher table. Three similar route handlers beat one cleverly parameterised one. |
| **P5 — OpenAPI-First** | `openapi.yaml` defines the 8 routes, the `RewriteStyle` enum, and the `TextRequest`/`TextResponse` schemas. The Angular client is generated; never hand-edited. Routes implement the contract — divergence is a build failure. |
| **P6 — Skills First** | Prompts live in SKILL.md files under the plugin's skills directory. Existing `brainstorm` and `rewrite` skills are reused; six new SKILL.md files are authored for the missing actions. |
| **P7 — File Size** | New `routes/text.py` blueprint stays under 200 LOC across 8 handlers. The rewritten `ai.service.ts` lands under 50 LOC as a thin wrapper over the generated client. |
| **Facade ownership** | Frontend has zero AI knowledge — no instruction strings, no system prompts, no `style` semantics. The `style` enum is a frontend label; its meaning lives in the rewrite SKILL.md. |

## Component Design

### OpenAPI Contract (`openapi.yaml`)

**Purpose**: Single source of truth for the 8 text-action routes, request/response shapes, and the `RewriteStyle` enum.

The contract defines `TextRequest` (always carries `text`), `RewriteRequest` (extends with `style`), and `BrainstormRequest` (extends with optional `question` and `context`). Response is uniform: `TextResponse { text: string, latencyMs: number }`. The `RewriteStyle` enum — `Concise | Technical | Executive | Narrative | Punchy` — lives here, so changes to allowed styles propagate to the generated client automatically. Routes are grouped under a `text` tag so `ng-openapi-gen` produces a coherent `TextService` client class.

### Flask Text Blueprint (`api/modules/ai/routes/text.py`)

**Purpose**: Eight thin route handlers — one per action — that map HTTP requests to skill invocations.

Each handler is auth-decorated, parses the JSON body into a typed dict, calls the corresponding skill via the chain adapter, captures `latencyMs` around the call, and returns the `TextResponse` shape. The brainstorm handler is the only one with conditional input (it forwards `question` and `context` if present); every other handler forwards `text` only, plus `style` for rewrite. No handler contains a prompt string, a Claude system message, or branching on action semantics — that's the whole point of the migration.

The blueprint replaces the legacy `/api/ai/text/rewrite` and `/api/ai/text/generate` routes once cutover is verified. The legacy `/api/ai/text/iterate`, `/lint-braindump`, and `/review` routes are out of scope — flagged for separate cleanup so this PR stays focused.

### Skill Layer (`plugin/skills/<action>/SKILL.md`)

**Purpose**: The prompt source of truth. One SKILL.md per text action.

Existing skills (`brainstorm`, `rewrite`) are reused as-is, with one extension: the brainstorm SKILL.md is updated to branch on the presence of `question` and `context` so the same skill handles both the bare brainstorm and the followup case currently assembled in `app.component.ts`. Six new SKILL.md files are authored — `expand`, `compress`, `clarify`, `simplify`, `tldr`, `bullets` — each containing the system prompt, user template, and any output formatting constraints previously hardcoded in `text_prompts.py`. Skills follow the existing reference pattern (When to use / What I do / Tools / Examples), with no rules duplicated inline that already live in `references/*.md`.

The rewrite SKILL.md owns the `style` semantics. The frontend sends the enum label; the skill maps `Concise → <instructions>`, `Technical → <instructions>`, etc. This mapping was the largest concentration of hidden coupling in the old design — moving it to a single Markdown file is the single biggest win of the phase.

### Chain Adapter Skill Invocation

**Purpose**: The bridge between Flask routes and Claude.

The adapter already exposes `generate()`, `rewrite()`, and `stream()`. Phase 3 invokes skills by routing through the existing `chain-agent` provider configuration — the SKILL.md path is selected by the route, and the adapter handles the subprocess (CLI provider) or SDK call (production). No new adapter primitive is added; we use what's there. This keeps the adapter boundary intact and avoids a speculative abstraction (P4).

### Generated Angular Client (`web-ng/src/app/api/`)

**Purpose**: Type-safe HTTP client produced from `openapi.yaml` by `ng-openapi-gen`, replacing the hand-written request layer.

The generator produces a `TextService` class with one method per route, fully typed against the schemas. Generated files are committed to the repo (so contributors don't need the generator installed for routine work) but never hand-edited. A npm script (`npm run generate:api`) regenerates them; CI fails if generated output is out of date with `openapi.yaml`.

### Thin AiService Wrapper (`web-ng/src/app/services/ai.service.ts`)

**Purpose**: Stable façade over the generated client, preserving the current call sites in components without forcing every consumer to migrate at once.

After Phase 3, `ai.service.ts` is a sub-50-LOC class with one method per action, each delegating to the generated `TextService`. It exists for two reasons: (1) it lets components keep calling `aiService.brainstorm(text)` instead of the generated `textService.postApiTextBrainstorm({ body: { text } })` shape, which is verbose; (2) it's the place to apply the global `AI_TIMEOUT_MS` and convert `Observable` to `Promise` (the current call style across components). No prompt logic. No instruction strings. No `style`-to-prompt mapping.

### Brainstorm-Followup Consolidation

**Purpose**: Eliminate the last instruction-string assembly site in the frontend.

`app.component.ts` currently builds a multi-line instruction string for followup brainstorms. Phase 3 collapses this into a single call to `aiService.brainstorm(text, { question, context })`. The brainstorm SKILL.md branches on `question` presence: empty → fresh brainstorm; present → followup mode that uses `context` as conversational state. The frontend ships zero awareness of which mode is active beyond passing the optional fields through.

## Technology Stack

| Layer | Choice | Rationale |
|-------|--------|-----------|
| API contract | OpenAPI 3.0 (`openapi.yaml`) | P5 — single source of truth; codegen on both sides; enum changes propagate automatically |
| Backend routes | Flask Blueprint (`/api/text`) | Matches existing project pattern; thin HTTP layer; auth decorator already in place |
| Prompt storage | SKILL.md files in plugin/skills/ | P6 — edit-without-deploy; one file per action; reuses existing skill infrastructure from Phase 2 |
| AI invocation | Existing chain adapter (`modules/runtime/chain/adapter.py`) | P1 — only AI call boundary; no new providers; CLI in dev, SDK in prod via env switch |
| Angular client codegen | `ng-openapi-gen` | Eliminates ~400 LOC of hand-written HTTP; type-safe against schema; standard tooling for OpenAPI + Angular |
| Frontend service | Thin `AiService` wrapper over generated client | Preserves call-site ergonomics; localises Promise/Observable conversion and timeout config |
| Background jobs | Out of scope (deferred to Phase 4) | Bootstrap and epic-guide chains stay on existing async 202 + polling pattern; not migrated this phase |

## Design Decisions

| Decision | Rationale | Trade-offs |
|----------|-----------|------------|
| Flat `/api/text/<action>` URL pattern | Matches the braindump's stated contract and the existing Angular sample shape; `text` namespace prevents collision with future non-text actions; consistent with how SKILL.md files are organised | The braindump's intro mentions even flatter URLs (`/api/brainstorm`); we settle on `/api/text/<action>` per the epic to keep namespace headroom for future action categories |
| Eight separate route handlers, no dispatcher | P4 — avoids a speculative `ActionRegistry`; each route is ~10 LOC and the duplication is mechanical; failures are localised; new actions follow a copy-paste-edit pattern rather than registering with a framework | ~30 LOC of duplicated handler boilerplate vs. one parameterised handler; we accept this because it makes the eight contracts independently auditable |
| `style` enum in OpenAPI, mapping in SKILL.md | Frontend gets type-safe labels via codegen; backend owns semantics; tweaking what "Concise" means to Claude is a Markdown edit, not a deploy | The frontend can no longer reason about prompt behaviour from its own code — it has to read SKILL.md to know what `style` actually does. This is the explicit goal (facade), not a regression. |
| Brainstorm and brainstorm-followup share one endpoint | Single SKILL.md branches on `question` presence; one route, one skill, one mental model; eliminates the last instruction-string assembly site in `app.component.ts` | The skill file gets a conditional branch; we accept this over two near-identical skills because the modes share most of their behaviour and inputs |
| Reuse existing chain adapter — no new primitive | P1 — the adapter already covers `generate`/`rewrite`/`stream`; routes call into the existing surface with the SKILL.md path selector | No special-cased "skill invocation" primitive. If skill invocation later needs distinct telemetry, we add it then — not speculatively. |
| Commit generated Angular client files | Routine contributors don't need the generator installed; PR diffs show what the contract change actually produced; CI catches drift | Generated files in version control inflate diff noise on contract changes; we mitigate with a clear `npm run generate:api` script and a CI drift check |
| Defer bootstrap and generate-epic-guide migration to Phase 4 | These are async multi-step chains; migrating them is materially harder than the eight one-shot text actions; bundling them risks blocking Phase 3's clear win | Two endpoints stay on the legacy `/api/ai/text/...` and `/api/projects/<id>/...` shape until Phase 4; the inconsistency is acknowledged and time-boxed |
| Delete `text_prompts.py`, `/api/ai/text/rewrite`, `/api/ai/text/generate` after cutover, in the same PR | Keeping legacy routes alive after cutover invites accidental reuse and obscures whether the migration is real; the PR proves the new path works by removing the old one | A larger blast radius if cutover regresses; mitigated by pre-cutover end-to-end verification and the fact that the old code stays in git history |
| Leave `iterate`, `lint-braindump`, `review` routes alone | They aren't called by the frontend; deleting them is unrelated cleanup that pollutes the Phase 3 PR | Dead code lingers one PR longer; flagged for follow-up |
| Leave `task_gen.py` and `quality/` untouched | Still used by active routes outside this phase's scope; auditing them properly requires its own pass | The braindump's "delete most of task_gen.py" goal is partially deferred; epic explicitly scopes this out |

## Related Documents

- [Analysis](./analysis.md) – Problems driving design
- [Epic](./epic.md) – Scope and tasks
- [Timeline](./timeline.md) – Status tracking
